title: Stream frame synchronizer and token-boundary detector to harden streaming toolcall boundaries
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: customer incidents and internal fuzzing showed streams where UTF-8 split tokens and out-of-order fragments caused function/toolcall sentinel tokens to be lost or misaligned, producing partial JSON blobs that could not be recovered by the existing reassembly layer. This PR introduces a lightweight stream frame synchronizer and an explicit token-boundary detector that together make the OpenAI-compat streaming layer resilient to: 1) UTF-8 split points across network frames, 2) late-arriving fragments that overlap previously emitted text, and 3) misordered event delivery due to retry/race scenarios.

Summary of changes (single-line): add frame synchronizer (Rust) + Python shim, token-boundary detector, heuristic watermarks for late-fragment reconciliation, updated toolcall sentinel handling, metrics and diagnostics, expanded fuzz/integration tests, docs.

What changed in code: implemented a stream/frame synchronizer in openai_compat/stream/frame_synchronizer.rs that maintains a compact rolling buffer and emits only UTF-8-complete frames; added a token_boundary detector which marks safe cut points for emitting events and for handing off KV-cache/toolcall sentinels; added a Python shim (openai_compat/stream/assembler.py) that integrates with the existing reassembly pipeline and converts frame-sync events into the original streaming consumer API; added late-fragment reconciliation logic that attempts to patch overlapping text when a fragment arrives with an earlier sequence id; added metrics: stream.synchronizer.resyncs, stream.synchronizer.late_patches, stream.token.boundary_errors; updated OpenAI compatibility adapter to use the new boundaries before running function-call detection; added doc page docs/openai-compat/streaming.md describing failure modes, recommended client backoff, and server-side compatibility knobs.

Compatibility notes: the new synchronizer is enabled by default on the OpenAI compatibility layer for streaming responses; it is a no-op for non-streaming endpoints. Behavior changes are limited to hardening against corrupted frames (should be transparent for well-behaved clients). Operators can disable the synchronizer per-route via ENABLE_FRAME_SYNC=false if necessary for debugging.

Testing & validation: unit tests for UTF-8 edge cases and token boundary identification; integration tests with the internal replay harness that simulates split/merged frames and reordered fragments; added a fuzz-based test (openai_compat/tests/fuzz_stream_reassembly.py) using property assertions that the assembled output is valid UTF-8 and that JSON object boundaries can be reconstituted or safely flagged for resync; added a small stress test to validate metrics and backpressure behavior under bursty client activity. CI shows the full matrix passing; local perf microbenchmarks indicate ~3%-5% CPU overhead in the compatibility shim with a 40–80% reduction in partial-JSON rescue events.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind the feature toggle ENABLE_FRAME_SYNC=true. We will deploy to canary cluster (region-us-west-2) for 48h with increased logging and sampling (trace rate 1%) and monitoring on stream.synchronizer.resyncs; if stable we will flip edge and dedicated regions sequentially over the next week.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for frame synchronizer and boundary detector
- [x] Integration tests with replay harness
- [x] Metrics and dashboards updated
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Reviewed and approved

Related: ENG-2345 (regression triage), SUP-712 (customer incident reproducer), ENG-2399 (follow-up to add persisted seq checksums).

release_notes: Fixes for streaming API: resilient frame reassembly and token-boundary detection to prevent partial JSON/toolcall corruption for split or reordered fragments. Enabled by default for OpenAI-compat streaming responses; operators can toggle off via ENABLE_FRAME_SYNC.
performance_impact: Microbenchmark: +3%-5% CPU on compatibility shim under synthetic load; reduces partial-json rescue events by ~40%-80% depending on workload. No measurable latency increase at p50; p95 shows +2-6ms in worst-case streams.
notes: Follow-ups: persist seq-checksums in ENG-2399, add per-route sampling for resync traces, and evaluate native-language shims for other SDKs.
